content.value_statement: Teams often skip tests until code is already complex. This skill keeps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code inside a clear TDD loop.
actual_capabilities: Guides work through red, green, and refactor phases.
Requires a failing test before production code.
Provides test naming guidance for behavior-focused tests.
Uses checklists to confirm tests fail and pass for the right reasons.
Shows TypeScript examples for incremental feature development.
limitations: It does not run tests by itself.
It does not choose framework-specific test commands.
It needs an existing project test setup.

use_cases.title: Add a Small Feature
use_cases.description: Plan the first failing test, write minimal code, and refactor only after the test passes.

use_cases.title: Coach Consistent TDD
use_cases.description: Keep team tasks aligned with the same red, green, and refactor checklist.

use_cases.title: Review Test Quality
use_cases.description: Check whether tests describe behavior instead of implementation details.

prompt_templates.title: Start a TDD Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this TDD workflow for the next feature. First list the simplest behavior, then write one failing test before any implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Make the First Test Pass
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a failing test. Suggest the smallest implementation that should pass it, and avoid extra behavior until another test requires it.

prompt_templates.title: Expand Coverage Incrementally
prompt_templates.scenario: Add edge cases after the first green state.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose the next test that forces a useful generalization. Keep each test focused on one behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor While Green
prompt_templates.prompt: All tests pass. Identify a small refactor, explain why behavior stays the same, and name the tests that protect the change.

output_examples.input: Add validation for blank email addresses.
output_examples.output: The assistant proposes one failing behavior test for blank input, then recommends the smallest validation change after the failure is confirmed.
The assistant confirms tests are green, names a focused refactor, and keeps the behavior covered by existing tests.

output_examples.input: Improve a test that checks private fields.
output_examples.output: The assistant reframes the test around observable behavior and suggests a clearer test name.

best_practices: Write one failing behavior test before editing production code.
Confirm each failure happens for the expected reason.
Refactor only when the full relevant test set is green.
anti_patterns: Writing production code before the first failing test.
Adding multiple tests before making the first one pass.
Testing private implementation details instead of user-visible behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill run my test suite?
faq.answer: No. It guides the TDD process, but your agent or environment must run the actual tests.

faq.question: Can I use it outside TypeScript projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is language neutral, although the examples use TypeScript syntax.

faq.question: Does it support refactoring work?
faq.answer: Yes. It encourages refactoring only after tests pass and after a specific improvement is identified.

faq.question: Will it write many tests at once?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks for one focused test, then implementation, then the next test.

faq.question: Is this useful with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. Claude Code can use the workflow to structure coding changes around tests.

faq.question: What makes this different from normal testing advice?
faq.answer: It enforces a strict order: failing test, minimal passing code, then refactor.
